research_question: Why is seven often considered lucky, and what can culture and psychology actually explain?

sources.title: Why 7 is the luckiest number
notes: Seven appears in calendars, religious traditions, games and popular culture.
The seven-day week and classical astronomical traditions helped make seven familiar.
The article treats explanations for preference as possibilities rather than proof of a universal law.

sources.title: The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two
sources.publisher: George A. Miller, York University Classics in Psychology
sources.reliability: Classic peer-reviewed psychology paper hosted by a university
notes: Miller examined limits in absolute judgement and immediate memory, not a supernatural property of seven.
The paper cautions against assuming several different cognitive limits are one process.
Miller suspected the many cultural sevens might be coincidence rather than a hidden universal rule.

sources.title: George Miller’s Magical Number of Immediate Memory in Retrospect
sources.publisher: Nelson Cowan, Psychological Review / PubMed Central
sources.reliability: Peer-reviewed psychology commentary hosted by NIH
notes: Miller's 1956 paper is often simplified in popular explanations.
Modern research distinguishes immediate memory capacity from other processing limits.
Historical context matters when interpreting the phrase 'magical number seven'.

sources.title: The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two: Some Limits on Our Capacity for Processing Information
sources.publisher: George A. Miller, Psychological Review PDF
notes: The 1956 article examined information-processing limits in several laboratory tasks.
Miller discussed chunking and strategies that change how much information can be handled.
The paper did not claim that seven is inherently lucky or supernatural.

sources.title: Why seven feels special: number symbolism and cultural repetition
notes: Seven's prominence reflects repeated appearances in calendars, traditions and cultural expressions.
The popularity of a number can be shaped by familiarity and reinforcement.
There is no scientific evidence that seven itself causes good fortune.
